reason: The original fast-Maker question requires a prescribed finite nonempty simple d-regular seed for every d with exp(o(d)) moves per vertex, yielding infinitely many graphs by disjoint-union amplification. This PR supplies a corrected exact seed reduction, elementary counting bounds and obstructions only to fixed-pool/full-activation or unprepared common-neighbor methods. It neither constructs the requested subexponential seed sequence nor proves a general negative theorem. Its conditional Gebauer benchmark is still 2^((2/3+o(1))d); component batching, adaptive role assignment and general strategies remain unexcluded. The two no-isolated-vertices patches fix subsidiary statements, not the original target.
